statement: A caller invoking a governed/catalog-driven service MUST NEVER unconditionally compute a public consequence projection (or any other projection-plane input) before dispatch. It must gate that computation on the resolved service definition's own declared need for it (e.g. `executionPolicy.executionReachable` / `projectionRequirement`) — the SAME condition the downstream orchestrator already uses to decide whether the projection is composed at all. When the input required to compute a real projection cannot be resolved from persisted/live data, the caller returns an explicit UNRESOLVED with a truthful reason; it never fabricates, backfills, or hardcodes a placeholder value merely to satisfy the code path.
classification: A caller/callee condition-duplication defect: the callee (`requestFinancialService`) already had the correct gating condition (`executionPolicy.executionReachable`) for whether a projection is needed, but the caller (the oversight route) computed the projection input unconditionally instead of reusing that same condition — so every non-executionReachable service paid the cost, and risk, of an unnecessary and structurally invalid computation.

canaries.assertion: An Advisor/Architect POST request never calls knowledgeCuration/forecastConsequences; a Runtime POST request resolves real persisted invariant UUIDs through the canonical invariant service (finance namespace) and resolves UNRESOLVED with an explicit reason — never a throw, never a hardcoded seed id — when none are live.

occurrences.defect: Called forecastConsequences(['inv.finance.001']) unconditionally before dispatching ANY financial service, including Advisor/Architect which declare projectionRequirement: 'NOT_REQUIRED' and never consume a forecast — and fed a human-readable seed id into a UUID-keyed graph API with no live match.

notes: A specialization of `inv.engineering.036`/`037` (one authoritative location per concern) applied to a CONDITION rather than a value: the gating condition for 'does this service need a projection' has exactly one correct home (the service definition's own policy fields), and any caller that re-derives or ignores that condition risks drifting from it.

Generic shape to watch for elsewhere: any caller that precomputes an expensive or fallible input 'just in case' before dispatch, rather than deferring to (or explicitly checking) the callee's own declared need for that input.
